pull.title: feat(harnesses): serve Command Code by merging one key into its config, and read the header it actually sends
pull.body:
## What this adds

`mcc-commandcode` — the seventh coding agent MCC can launch, speaking Anthropic
Messages against `POST /v1/messages`. Registry entry, launcher, catalogue
serialiser, console script, both installers and both uninstallers, `mcc-help`,
the Coding agents card, README / `docs/USAGE.md` / `ARCHITECTURE.md` / Guide /
Get Started — all generated from the one `HarnessSpec`.

## Why it needed a new mechanism

Command Code is the first CLI MCC can serve **only** by writing into a file the
user owns. Read out of the installed binary's own bundle (`command-code`
1.39.0, `dist/cli.mjs`):

```js
function homeDir15(e){return e.env().HOME??e.env().USERPROFILE}
function getUserProvidersConfigPath(e){const t=homeDir15(e.runtime);
  return t?`${t}/.commandcode/providers.json`:void 0}
```

and `loadProvidersConfig` reads that path and nothing else — no `--config`
flag, no config environment variable, no project-local file. Every other
harness has an escape (two env vars for Claude Code, ephemeral `-c` for Codex,
a process-local registration for Pi, `OPENCODE_CONFIG` / `KILO_CONFIG` for the
OpenCode family). This one does not, so PR spec Q14's merge path applies.

`config/harness_config_merge.py` is the only module in the codebase allowed to
write a document MCC did not create, and it makes four guarantees, each pinned
by a test:

| Guarantee | Test |
| --- | --- |
| One key — only `provider.mcc` is written; everything else is carried through | `test_every_key_mcc_did_not_write_survives_byte_for_byte` |
| One backup, taken before the first edit and never refreshed | `test_the_backup_is_the_users_file_not_yesterdays_mcc_output` |
| Idempotent, measured on MCC's key rather than the file's bytes | `test_an_unchanged_refresh_writes_nothing_and_backs_nothing_up`, `test_a_users_own_indentation_is_not_reformatted_on_an_unchanged_refresh` |
| Reversible — `mcc-commandcode --disconnect` | `test_disconnect_removes_only_mccs_key` |

The comparison is on the owned subtree and not on the file's bytes on purpose:
the atomic writer emits one canonical two-space shape, so a byte comparison
would reformat the whole document of anyone who indents differently, on every
single launch.

The background fan-out is stricter still — it keys off the **presence of MCC's
own key**, never the file's existence. A Command Code user who has never run
`mcc-commandcode` already has a `providers.json`, and finding a `provider.mcc`
block appear in it because a provider key rotated on a server they left running
is exactly what the never-write-for-an-unlaunched-harness rule exists to stop
(`test_a_users_own_config_is_not_written_into_until_mcc_is_invited`).

Home is resolved the way the *CLI* resolves it (`HOME` first, `USERPROFILE`
second), not the way `Path.home()` does on Windows. A developer with `HOME` set
— every Git-for-Windows install — would otherwise have MCC merge into one file
while the CLI read another, with a picker that silently never shows MCC's
models as the only symptom.

## The token still never lands on disk

`providers.json` refuses a literal key ("raw secrets don't belong in
providers.json") and expands `"$VAR"` from the process environment instead, so
the merged block carries `"$MCC_COMMANDCODE_API_KEY"` and the launcher sets it
in the child process only. `baseURL` *is* written literally: Command Code
validates that field with `new URL(...)` and substitutes nothing into it. The
serialiser is a pure function of the model records and cannot know this
install's port, so it emits `COMMANDCODE_BASE_URL_SENTINEL` and the caller —
launcher or publisher, both of which know the proxy root — replaces it before
the block reaches disk.

## One change outside the harness layer: the auth header

`require_proxy_auth` read `Authorization: Bearer` only. Command Code's
`authHeadersFor` sends `{"x-api-key": key}` and **nothing else** for a provider
declared `api: "anthropic-messages"`, and its static `headers` map takes no
substitution — so the trick PR #244 used for OpenCode (write an explicit bearer
header) would have put the proxy token into the user's own file. Both headers
are how a real Anthropic Messages client authenticates, so MCC now reads both,
with `Authorization` still winning when both are present and
`anthropic-auth-token` still unread.

## Serialiser mapping

`application/catalogues/commandcode.py`, every field read out of `parseModel` /
`parseProvider` / `parseCost` in Command Code's own bundle:

| Ladder | Command Code |
| --- | --- |
| `context_length` | `contextWindow` |
| `max_output_tokens` | `maxOutput` |
| `reasoning.can_reason` | `reasoning` |
| `reasoning.supported_efforts` | `reasoningEfforts[]`, intersected with `low\|medium\|high\|xhigh\|max` and never extended |
| `input_price` / `output_price` | `cost.input` / `cost.output` (models.dev units, which is where both come from) |
| `default_parameters` | `options` |

Unknown stays unknown: every key is optional, so a `None` omits it and the
omission is recorded under `_mcc_defaulted` — folded **inside** `provider.mcc`,
so removing MCC's key removes every trace of MCC — printed on the launcher's
stderr and counted on the dashboard card. What Command Code does instead of an
absent key (`maxOutput` falls back to `max(1024, contextWindow/2)`) is recorded
in `CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS`, read out of its bundle rather than guessed, and
`test_no_serialiser_hard_codes_a_limit` AST-scans the module.

One real generated fragment, from the scratch run:

```json
"mcc": {
  "name": "My Claude Code",
  "api": "anthropic-messages",
  "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8199/v1",
  "apiKey": "$MCC_COMMANDCODE_API_KEY",
  "models": {
    "custom_scratch/scratch-big":   {"name": "custom_scratch/scratch-big",   "maxOutput": 54321, "reasoning": true},
    "custom_scratch/scratch-small": {"name": "custom_scratch/scratch-small", "maxOutput": 4096,  "reasoning": false}
  },
  "_mcc_defaulted": {
    "custom_scratch/scratch-big":   ["contextWindow", "reasoningEfforts", "cost"],
    "custom_scratch/scratch-small": ["contextWindow", "cost"]
  }
}
```

Two models, two different `maxOutput` values and two different reasoning
answers — which a fixed placeholder cannot produce.

## Harness id vs provider id

The harness is `commandcode_cli`, not `commandcode`. The latter is already an
**upstream gateway provider** in `config/provider_catalog.py`, and both halves
ship in this release: one is where MCC can buy tokens, the other is a CLI MCC
serves. `opencode` and `kilo` are allowed to overlap and the README says why;
Command Code is the one case where the same string would resolve a harness and
a provider in the same release, so the suffix removes the collision
(`test_the_command_code_harness_id_never_collides_with_the_gateway_provider`).
The distinction is written out in the same boxed paragraph PR #244 added, in
both `README.md` and `docs/USAGE.md` §6.

## Real launch proof

Scratch MCC on **8199** with `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` redirected to a scratch
home, fed by a local gateway on **8299**, with a seeded models.dev cache so the
ladder had offline answers. The user's real `~/.commandcode` was never read or
written and holds no `providers.json`.

```
$ mcc-commandcode --list-models
My Claude Code: Created provider.mcc in ...\home\.commandcode\providers.json.
My Claude Code: 2 model(s) publish no value for one or more fields, so Command Code falls back to its own default:
  custom_scratch/scratch-big: contextWindow, reasoningEfforts, cost
  custom_scratch/scratch-small: contextWindow, cost
...
My Claude Code (byok)
mcc/custom_scratch/scratch-big         custom_scratch/scratch-big
mcc/custom_scratch/scratch-small       custom_scratch/scratch-small

$ mcc-commandcode -p "say ok" -m mcc/custom_scratch/scratch-big --max-turns 1
OK from the scratch gateway.
```

MCC's own request log for that turn:

```json
{"endpoint": "/v1/messages", "protocol": "anthropic",
 "requested_model": "custom_scratch/scratch-big", "provider": "custom_scratch",
 "resolved_model": "scratch-big", "status": "success",
 "headers": {"user-agent": "ai-sdk/anthropic/3.0.115 ai-sdk/provider-utils/4.0.50 runtime/node.js/24",
             "(unlisted)": "...,x-api-key"}}
```

`x-api-key` and no `authorization` — the header Command Code actually sends,
now read. Direct check on the same server: `x-api-key: <right token>` → 200,
`x-api-key: nope` → 401.

Then, with the user's own `ollama` provider and a `theme` key added to the
file: a second `--list-models` left it **byte-identical** and took no backup,
and `mcc-commandcode --disconnect` removed `provider.mcc` and left `ollama` and
`theme` exactly as they were.

## The card's command list

`mcc-commandcode` · `mcc-commandcode -p "<prompt>"` ·
`mcc-commandcode --list-models` · `mcc-commandcode -m mcc/<provider>/<model>` ·
`mcc-commandcode --local-only` · `mcc-commandcode --disconnect`. No `fcc-`
alias, and no RTK toggle — RTK's shell-tool wrapper is unverified for this
agent, so `rtk_agent=False`. Passthrough (no proxy needed, no config written):
`update`, `login`, `logout`, `mcp`, `skills`, `mods`, `taste`, `status`,
`info`, `whoami`, `feedback`, `--help`, `--version`.

## Browser drive

`http://127.0.0.1:8199/admin` → Coding agents. Screenshots in
`screenshots-harness-pr5/`.

| Checked | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Cards rendered | 7, in registry order, Command Code last |
| Command Code state | **Installed**, `/usr/local/bin`-style path probed via `shutil.which` |
| Command list | all six lines, each with a working copy button |
| Protocol row | Anthropic Messages (POST /v1/messages) |
| Config file row | the user's own `~/.commandcode/providers.json`, not a `~/.fcc` path |
| Last written / Models | `2026-09-01T22:19:10.149018Z` / `2` |
| Merged key row | `provider.mcc - the only key MCC writes; every other key is left byte-for-byte, and your file is backed up before the first edit` |
| CLI defaults row | `2 model(s) carry a value Command Code supplied because no provider published one` |
| Console errors | zero (one pre-existing a11y *issue* notice, no errors) |
| Horizontal overflow | none (`scrollWidth <= clientWidth`) |

## Tests

New: `tests/application/test_commandcode_serialiser.py` (13),
`tests/config/test_harness_config_merge.py` (15),
`tests/cli/test_commandcode_launcher.py` (8). Extended:
`tests/cli/test_harness_registry.py` (+3 and two rewritten for the new
`delivery` field), `tests/runtime/test_catalogue_fanout.py` (+3),
`tests/api/test_admin_harnesses.py` (+2), `tests/api/test_dependencies.py`
(+2, one rewritten), `tests/api/test_auth.py` (2 rewritten),
`tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` (+1), `tests/scripts/test_installers.py`
(fake `uv tool install` stub lists, both platforms).

- Full suite: **8157 passed, 38 skipped, 15 failed** — the documented
  pre-existing local baseline (`websearch/*`, `test_web_server_tools` ×2,
  `install.ps1` ×6, `test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`),
  none touched by this change.
- jsdom alone with `-n 0`: **186 passed** (185 before, +1 here).
- `ruff format`, `ruff check`, `ty check` clean over `src/` and `tests/`.

## Residual risks

- **The merge is a merge.** MCC now writes into a file the user owns. The
  guarantees above are tested, but a document with a *non-object* `provider`
  value is replaced rather than merged into (Command Code would reject it
  anyway), and a real content change rewrites the whole document in the atomic
  writer's two-space shape — the backup is the mitigation, and the unchanged
  case no longer touches the file at all.
- **Accepting `x-api-key` widens the accepted auth surface** by one header.
  It still requires the exact configured token, compared with
  `secrets.compare_digest`, and `Authorization` still wins when both are
  present — but it is a behaviour change to a security-relevant path and two
  tests that asserted the old rejection were deliberately rewritten.
- **`contextWindow` and `cost` were `null` in the scratch run**, because a
  custom provider can only reach the cross-provider reference rung and this
  machine had no live models.dev feed. That is the ladder's existing behaviour,
  not the serialiser's — the mapping for those two keys is covered by unit
  test rather than by the live run.
- **`reasoningEfforts` was never populated in the live run** for the same
  reason. Its clamping is covered by four unit tests, not by a real model.
- **Command Code auto-updates itself.** The launcher passes nothing to stop
  that; a user's `command-code` may change schema under a generated block. The
  serialiser was read against 1.39.0 and the version is stated in every
  docstring so the next reader knows what to re-check.
- **`--disconnect` is MCC's flag, not Command Code's.** If a future Command
  Code release adds a flag of that name, the launcher would shadow it. Checked
  against 1.39.0's full `--help`: no collision today.

commit.message:
feat(harnesses): serve Command Code by merging one key into its config, and read the header it actually sends

Command Code is the first CLI MCC can serve only by writing into a file the
user owns. Every other harness has an escape: Claude Code takes two environment
variables, Codex ephemeral -c assignments, Pi a process-local registration, and
the OpenCode family an *extra* config file named by its own OPENCODE_CONFIG /
KILO_CONFIG variable. Command Code 1.39.0 has none. Its bundled dist/cli.mjs
reads exactly one document --

    function homeDir15(e){return e.env().HOME??e.env().USERPROFILE}
    function getUserProvidersConfigPath(e){const t=homeDir15(e.runtime);
      return t?`${t}/.commandcode/providers.json`:void 0}

-- and loadProvidersConfig reads that path and no other: no --config flag, no
config environment variable, no project-local file. So the choice was to merge
or to not ship the harness.

It merges, through one new module that is the only place in this codebase
allowed to write a document MCC did not create, with four guarantees each
pinned by a test. One key: only provider.mcc is written, and every other key is
read, carried through and written back unchanged. One backup: the document is
copied to providers.json.mcc-backup before MCC's first edit and never
afterwards, so the copy is always the user's pre-MCC file rather than
yesterday's MCC output. Idempotent, and deliberately measured on MCC's key
rather than on the file's bytes -- the atomic writer emits one canonical
two-space shape, so a byte comparison would reformat the whole document of
anyone who indents differently, on every launch. And reversible:
mcc-commandcode --disconnect deletes the key and leaves the rest exactly as it
was. The background fan-out is stricter still: it keys off the presence of
MCC's own key, never the file's existence, because a Command Code user who has
never run mcc-commandcode already has a providers.json and must not find a
provider block in it because a key rotated on a server they left running.

The proxy token still never lands on disk. providers.json refuses a literal key
-- "raw secrets don't belong in providers.json" -- and expands "$VAR" from the
process environment instead, so the merged block carries
"$MCC_COMMANDCODE_API_KEY" and the launcher sets it in the child only. baseURL
is written literally, because Command Code validates that field with new URL()
and substitutes nothing into it; the serialiser is a pure function of the model
records and cannot know this install's port, so it emits a sentinel and the
caller -- launcher or publisher, both of which know the proxy root -- replaces
it before the block reaches disk.

That block also forced the one change outside the harness layer.
require_proxy_auth read Authorization: Bearer only, while Command Code's
authHeadersFor sends {"x-api-key": key} and nothing else for a provider
declared api: "anthropic-messages", and its static headers map takes no
substitution -- so the OpenCode trick of writing an explicit bearer header
would have put the token in the user's own file. Both headers are how a real
Anthropic Messages client authenticates, so MCC now reads both, Authorization
still winning when both are present. Measured: x-api-key with the right token
200, with a wrong one 401, anthropic-auth-token still unread.

application/catalogues/commandcode.py follows the rules the other serialisers
obey. contextWindow, maxOutput, reasoning, reasoningEfforts, cost and options
come from the ladder; reasoningEfforts is intersected with Command Code's own
low|medium|high|xhigh|max and never extended. Unknown stays unknown: every key
is optional, so a None omits it, and the omission is recorded under
_mcc_defaulted -- folded inside provider.mcc so removing MCC's key removes every
trace of MCC -- printed on the launcher's stderr and counted on the dashboard
card. What Command Code does instead of an absent key (maxOutput falls back to
max(1024, contextWindow/2)) is documented in CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS, read out
of its own bundle rather than guessed.

The harness id is commandcode_cli, not commandcode. The latter is already an
upstream gateway provider in this codebase, and both halves ship: one is where
MCC can buy tokens, the other is a CLI MCC serves. A shared id would let a
lookup for one silently answer for the other.

Verification. Scratch MCC on 8199 with HOME and USERPROFILE redirected, fed by
a local gateway on 8299, and a seeded models.dev cache so the ladder had real
answers. mcc-commandcode --list-models created provider.mcc, printed which
fields nobody published, and Command Code listed both models under "My Claude
Code (byok)". mcc-commandcode -p "say ok" -m mcc/custom_scratch/scratch-big
returned the gateway's reply, and MCC's request log recorded endpoint
/v1/messages, protocol anthropic, requested_model custom_scratch/scratch-big,
user-agent ai-sdk/anthropic/3.0.115 runtime/node.js/24, headers carrying
x-api-key and no authorization, status success. Two models, two different
maxOutput values (54321 and 4096) and two different reasoning answers, which
fixed placeholders could not produce. A second --list-models with the user's
own ollama provider and theme key present rewrote nothing and left the file
byte-identical; --disconnect removed provider.mcc and left ollama and theme
exactly as they were. The user's real ~/.commandcode was never read or written.

Full suite 8157 passed with the same 15 pre-existing failures that fail on
unmodified fork/main; jsdom suite 186 passed alone with -n 0. Browser-driven on
the Coding agents page: seven cards, Command Code installed, its six command
lines with working copy buttons, the config-file path, timestamp, model count,
the Merged key row and the CLI-defaults count, zero console errors.

Deliberately not done: MCC does not set CMD_LOCAL_ONLY or supply a Command Code
credential. Its headless -p mode checks you are signed in to Command Code
before it runs a turn, whatever model you asked for; that belongs to Command
Code's account, not to this proxy, and is documented rather than worked around.

style(tests): run the formatter over the four test files that were appended to

Three of the new test files and one extension were written with an append
rather than an editor, after the last repo-wide `ruff format` of the session,
and the per-file formatting runs afterwards did not cover them. `ruff-format`
is check-only in CI, so it caught what the local repair-mode run had already
silently fixed elsewhere. No behaviour change: `ruff check`, `ty` and the four
files' 34 tests pass identically before and after.
